title: Prime-power depth of arbitrary bent partitions
summary: Determine whether the depth of every bent partition is a power of the underlying field characteristic.

formal_statement.body: Let $p$ be prime and let $\Gamma=\{A_1,\ldots,A_K\}$ be a bent partition of $V_n^{(p)}$ in the source sense, with the source's admissible dimension convention. Must $K=p^r$ for some integer $r\ge 1$? Equivalently, prove the prime-power property for every bent partition or construct one whose depth is not a power of $p$.

scope.domain: Bent partitions and p-ary or vectorial bent functions
assumptions: n is even except for the source's p = K = 3 case
Bent partition and depth K use the source definitions
scope.unresolved_remainder: The source proves the claim for weakly regular bent partitions. arXiv:2606.27776 proves it for the strict odd-prime symmetric subclass with K >= 5 and -A_i = A_i. Arbitrary bent partitions outside these subclasses remain unresolved.

citations.label: Wang--Wei--Fu, further results on bent partitions
citations.locator: Abstract and Introduction, p. 3447; Theorem 3 and conclusion, pp. 3451-3459

progress.summary: The source proves prime-power depth for its weakly regular subclass and explicitly leaves the all-partitions statement open.
citation_labels: Wang--Wei--Fu, further results on bent partitions

progress.summary: A later preprint proves prime-power depth for odd-prime bent partitions satisfying K >= 5 and -A_i = A_i, a strict subclass of the original question.
